name: Norse & Celtic Mythology
description: Questions covering: Norse Mythology, Norse Cosmology, Celtic Mythology, Comparative Mythology...

questions.question: Which Norse god is associated with wisdom, poetry, ravens, and the hall Valhalla?
questions.explanation_correct: Odin is a prominent Norse god associated with wisdom, war, poetry and Valhalla; religious prominence varied across places and periods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Thor, Loki and Njord are other Norse figures, but Odin is associated with the named hall and ravens.

questions.question: Which Norse god is known as the thunder god?
questions.explanation_correct: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, storms, and strength. He is commonly depicted wielding the hammer Mjölnir.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Odin is the chief god, Heimdall guards Bifröst, and Loki is a trickster, so they are not the thunder god.

questions.question: Which shape-shifting Norse figure is known for deceiving the gods and causing mischief?
questions.explanation_correct: Loki is the Norse trickster figure, known for mischief, deception, and shape-shifting. He plays a disruptive role in many myths.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Odin also uses disguise and deception in myths, but Loki is the figure described by the combination of clues.

questions.question: What is the name of the world tree in Norse cosmology?
questions.explanation_correct: Yggdrasil is the great cosmic tree that connects the worlds in Norse cosmology. It is central to the structure of the mythological universe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bifröst is a bridge, Valhalla is a hall, and Asgard is a realm, so they are not the world tree.

questions.question: What is the name of Odin’s hall, where many warriors slain in battle are received?
questions.explanation_correct: Valhalla is Odin’s hall for slain warriors; Freyja also receives a share of the slain in another account.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Yggdrasil is a tree, Bifröst a bridge, and Asgard a realm.

questions.question: What is the name of the bridge that connects to Asgard in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Bifröst is the shimmering bridge that links the worlds and leads to Asgard. It is often described as a rainbow bridge.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Valhalla is a hall, Yggdrasil is the world tree, and Midgard is the human realm, so they are not the bridge.

questions.question: Which Norse god serves as the guardian of Bifröst?
questions.explanation_correct: Heimdall is the watchful god who guards Bifröst and keeps vigil for threats. He is associated with keen senses and alertness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Odin is the chief god, Thor is the thunder god, and Loki is a trickster, so they are not the guardian of the bridge.

questions.question: Which Norse deity is associated with the sea?
questions.explanation_correct: Njord is the Norse god associated with the sea, seafaring, and wealth. He is linked to maritime prosperity and calm waters.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Thor is tied to thunder, Heimdall guards Bifröst, and Odin is the chief god, so they are not the sea god.

questions.question: Which Irish deity is known as the sea god?
questions.explanation_correct: Manannán is an Irish sea deity associated with the ocean, otherworldly travel, and protection. He appears in many Irish mythological traditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Morrígan is associated with battle; Lugh is a divine figure and Cú Chulainn a hero in Irish tradition.

questions.question: Which Irish figure, associated with battle, appears to the hero Cú Chulainn in the Táin Bó Cúailnge?
questions.explanation_correct: The Morrígan is a supernatural figure associated with battle and fate who appears in the Táin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brigid, Danu and Ériu are different figures in Irish tradition; associations with sovereignty can overlap.

questions.question: Which supernatural people defeat the Fir Bolg at the first Battle of Mag Tuired in Irish tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: The Tuatha Dé Danann defeat the Fir Bolg in the first Battle of Mag Tuired in the medieval Irish invasion narratives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Fomorians and Fir Bolg also appear in traditions predating the Milesians, but are different groups.

questions.question: Which warrior is the central hero of the Ulster Cycle?
questions.explanation_correct: Cú Chulainn is the foremost hero associated with the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology. He appears in the Táin Bó Cúailnge and related tales.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names belong to different figures from Irish legend or do not fit this heroic role. They are not the Ulster Cycle's principal champion.

questions.question: What is the name of the Welsh otherworld associated with mystical travel and the dead?
questions.explanation_correct: Annwn is the Welsh otherworld in mythology and medieval literature. It is often depicted as a hidden realm of abundance, mystery, or the dead.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other mythic realms from different traditions or contexts. They are not the Welsh otherworld asked for here.

questions.question: In the First Branch of the Mabinogi, which ruler of Annwn exchanges places with Pwyll?
questions.explanation_correct: Arawn exchanges appearances and places with Pwyll for a year in the First Branch.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gwyn ap Nudd is also associated with the Otherworld in Welsh tradition; Arawn is the ruler in this particular tale.

questions.question: Which Irish festival is associated with the beginning of the harvest season?
questions.explanation_correct: Lughnasadh is one of the four major Gaelic seasonal festivals and marks the start of the harvest. It is traditionally linked to Lugh.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also seasonal festivals, but they mark different points in the year. They do not correspond to the harvest festival requested.

questions.question: Which creature is the giant serpent encircling the world in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Jormungandr is the Midgard Serpent, so large that it surrounds the world in Norse cosmology. It is a major foe of Thor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different beings from Norse myth, including a dragon, a horse, and a wolf-like guardian. They are not the world-encircling serpent.

questions.question: Which bound wolf is foretold to swallow Odin at Ragnarök?
questions.explanation_correct: Fenrir is bound by the gods and, in the Prose Edda’s account of Ragnarök, kills Odin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sköll is another wolf involved in Ragnarök traditions; Geri and Freki are Odin’s wolves.

questions.question: Which daughter of Loki presides over the realm called Hel in the Prose Edda?
questions.explanation_correct: Hel is a daughter of Loki and presides over the realm bearing her name in the Prose Edda.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Freyja also receives a share of those slain in battle; she is not the figure ruling the realm called Hel.

questions.question: What are the names of Odin's two ravens?
questions.explanation_correct: Huginn and Muninn are Odin's ravens, representing thought and memory. They fly across the world and bring back information to him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are paired figures from Norse myth, but they are not Odin's ravens. They refer to wolves, wolves associated with the sun and moon, or dwarven smiths.

questions.question: Which husband of Iðunn is described as a god of poetry and eloquence?
questions.explanation_correct: Bragi is the Norse god associated with poetry, skaldic verse, and eloquence. He is often described as a divine poet.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Odin is also associated with poetry, but Bragi is identified here by his marriage to Iðunn.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, what is the name of the horse associated with the bridge guardian Heimdall?
questions.explanation_correct: Gulltoppr is the horse associated with Heimdall in Norse myth. Heimdall is the guardian of the Bifröst bridge.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also names of horses from myth, but they are linked to different figures. None is Heimdall's horse.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, who is the sea giant associated with a hall where feasts are held?
questions.explanation_correct: Aegir is the sea giant known for hosting feasts in his hall. He is closely associated with the sea and brewing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also Norse figures connected to the sea, poetry, or the gods, but they are not the hall-holding sea giant.

questions.question: What is the name of the Irish Otherworld whose name means “Land of Youth”?
questions.explanation_correct: Tir na nOg is the Celtic Otherworld associated with eternal youth and beauty. It appears in Irish legend.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Otherworld realms overlap in attributes, but Tír na nÓg is the name that specifically means Land of Youth.

questions.question: Which Irish hero is traditionally linked to gaining wisdom from the Salmon of Knowledge?
questions.explanation_correct: Fionn mac Cumhaill is the hero who gained wisdom after tasting the Salmon of Knowledge. This tale is a central Irish myth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major Irish heroes, but they are not the one associated with the Salmon of Knowledge. Their legends involve different feats and episodes.

questions.question: Which woman in the First Branch of the Mabinogi marries Pwyll and becomes the mother of Pryderi?
questions.explanation_correct: Rhiannon, associated with a remarkable horse, marries Pwyll and is the mother of Pryderi. Her interpretation as a goddess is scholarly rather than a title the medieval tale always gives her.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Blodeuwedd, Arianrhod and Ceridwen are other figures in Welsh tradition.

questions.question: In an Irish tale, whose four children are transformed into swans by their stepmother Aoife?
questions.explanation_correct: Lir is the father of the children in the tale; their stepmother Aoife transforms them into swans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Manannán, Balor and the Dagda are different figures in Irish traditions.

questions.question: Which figure is the skilled divine smith of the Tuatha Dé Danann?
questions.explanation_correct: Goibniu is the divine smith of the Tuatha Dé Danann. He is associated with craft and forging.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are major Tuatha Dé Danann figures, but they are not the smith. Their roles are tied to kingship, skill, or war.

questions.question: Which Welsh giant-king is said to have his head buried in London as a protective charm?
questions.explanation_correct: Bran the Blessed is the giant king of Welsh tradition whose severed head is buried to protect Britain. He appears in the Mabinogion.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Welsh mythic kings or rulers, but they are not the giant king with that burial tradition. Their stories differ in setting and function.

questions.question: Which Celtic festival marks the end of the harvest season and the start of winter?
questions.explanation_correct: Samhain is a Gaelic seasonal festival traditionally associated with the beginning of winter and the end of the harvest period. Tales also connect it with encounters with supernatural beings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are important Gaelic festivals, but they mark different seasonal points. They are not the traditional harvest-ending festival.

questions.question: Which Irish goddess gave her name to the island of Ireland in tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: Eriu is the Irish sovereignty goddess whose name is associated with Ireland. The island's name is linked to her in tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are major Irish goddesses, but they are not the one directly tied to the island's name. Their roles are different in myth and legend.

questions.question: Which figure is the messenger squirrel in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Ratatoskr is the squirrel who runs messages up and down Yggdrasil. He is a well-known figure in Norse mythic lore.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a horse, a god, and a sea goddess, not a messenger squirrel.

questions.question: Which horse carries the goddess Gná through the air and over the sea in the Prose Edda?
questions.explanation_correct: Hófvarpnir is the horse of Gná, a messenger of Frigg; Heimdall’s horse is called Gulltoppr.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Álfheimr is a realm, Kvasir a wise being, and Freyja a goddess.

questions.question: Which Norse god loses a hand when the gods bind Fenrir?
questions.explanation_correct: Týr places his hand in Fenrir’s mouth as a pledge and loses it when the wolf discovers he has been bound.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different beings from Norse and Welsh traditions.

questions.question: Which Norse sea goddess is known for capturing sailors?
questions.explanation_correct: Ran is the sea goddess who catches drowned sailors in a net. She is closely tied to the dangerous aspects of the sea.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a goddess of magic and love, a Celtic sea deity, and a figure connected to poetry mead.

questions.question: Which figure is credited with the origin of the mead of poetry in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Kvasir is the wise being whose blood becomes the basis for the mead of poetry. This makes him central to that mythic origin story.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a god, a horse, and a Welsh Otherworld ruler, not the source of the mead of poetry.

questions.question: What is the name of the Norse realm of the elves?
questions.explanation_correct: Alfheim is the realm associated with the elves in Norse cosmology. It is one of the traditional worlds of the mythic universe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a goddess, a squirrel, and a sea god, not a world of the elves.

questions.question: Which Norse goddess is also associated with seiðr and prophecy?
questions.explanation_correct: Freyja is a major Norse goddess linked to seiðr, fertility, and prophecy. She is often connected with magical and divinatory practice.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a male god of justice, a divine smith, and a being tied to poetry mead, not a vǫlva-associated goddess.

questions.question: Which figure associated with Annwn leads supernatural hounds in Welsh tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: Gwyn ap Nudd is associated with Annwn and supernatural hunts in Welsh tradition; accounts of the Otherworld have more than one ruler.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Arawn is another ruler of Annwn in a different tale; the listed alternatives do not identify Gwyn.

questions.question: What is the Welsh name of the father of Brân the Blessed and Branwen?
questions.explanation_correct: Llŷr is a figure in Welsh tradition and father of Brân and Branwen; Irish Lir is a related name in a separate tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gofannon, Ratatoskr and Freyja are other figures; the name Llŷr belongs to Welsh tradition.

questions.question: Which Celtic deity is a divine smith?
questions.explanation_correct: Gofannon is the divine smith in Welsh/Celtic mythology. He is associated with craftsmanship and metalworking.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a Norse god, a sea goddess, and a horse, not a smith deity.

questions.question: Which Celtic deity is associated with horses and cavalry?
questions.explanation_correct: Epona is the Celtic horse goddess, especially associated with horses, stables, and riding. She was widely worshiped in Gaul and later in the Roman world.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a sun/healing god, an Irish queen, and a spring festival, not a horse deity.

questions.question: Which ancestral figure is named as the father of Lludd and Llefelys in a Welsh tale?
questions.explanation_correct: Beli Mawr is named as the father of Lludd and Llefelys in the Welsh tale of the two brothers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Frigg, Freyr and Ymir belong to Norse tradition, not Welsh genealogies.

questions.question: Which Irish figure is closely linked to sovereignty and kingship?
questions.explanation_correct: Medb is an important Irish sovereignty figure associated with rule, power, and royal legitimacy. She appears prominently in the Ulster Cycle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are a horse goddess, a Welsh king, and a seasonal festival rather than an Irish sovereignty figure.

questions.question: What is the Celtic festival marking the beginning of spring?
questions.explanation_correct: Imbolc is one of the traditional Celtic seasonal festivals and is associated with the start of spring. It is often connected with Brigid and purification.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options name a realm of the dead, a deity, and a Norse goddess, not a spring festival.

questions.question: Which Celtic deity was identified with Apollo in some Roman inscriptions?
questions.explanation_correct: Belenus is a Celtic deity identified with Apollo in Roman sources; precise interpretations of his attributes vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lugh is also a complex deity with diverse associations, but the question concerns the attested Apollo-Belenus identification.

questions.question: Who is the wife of Odin in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Frigg is Odin's wife and one of the major goddesses in Norse myth. She is associated with foresight, marriage, and motherhood.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are a fertility god and figures from Celtic mythology, not Odin's spouse.

questions.question: Which Norse god is associated with fertility and prosperity?
questions.explanation_correct: Freyr is a Vanir god strongly associated with fertility, prosperity, and peace. He is one of the most important gods in the Norse pantheon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a goddess, a Celtic sun god, and a Welsh king, so they do not match this description.

questions.question: What is Bifröst described as in the Prose Edda?
options: A bridge between heaven and earth
questions.answer: A bridge between heaven and earth
questions.explanation_correct: The Prose Edda describes Bifröst as a bridge connecting earth and heaven, built by the gods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gungnir is Odin’s spear and Gleipnir is the wolf’s fetter; the cauldron is another object.

questions.question: Which Norse realm is associated with the deepest underworld of the dead?
questions.explanation_correct: Niflhel is a dark underworld realm in Norse cosmology associated with the dead. It is often treated as a deeper or more remote level beneath Hel.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are the gods' stronghold, the Vanir's homeland, and the elves' realm rather than the underworld.

questions.question: Who is the primeval frost giant in Norse creation myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Ymir is the primordial giant whose body is used to make the world in a Norse creation account; the primeval cow Auðhumla also appears early in that story.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a goddess, a fertility god, and a Celtic deity, not the primeval giant.

questions.question: Which dwarf worked with Brokkr to make Mjölnir in the tale told in the Prose Edda?
questions.explanation_correct: In the Prose Edda’s account Brokkr works with his brother Sindri; Eitri appears in related textual discussion and traditions, so the earlier pair of alternatives was ambiguous.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other dwarfs are associated with other stories; Sindri is Brokkr’s brother in the specified account.

questions.question: Which Norse god presides over the hall Glitnir, associated specifically with justice and reconciliation?
questions.explanation_correct: Forseti is the Norse god linked with justice, mediation, and his hall at Glitnir, where he settles disputes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Tyr is associated with the assembly and law, Glitnir is specifically the hall of Forseti.

questions.question: Which Welsh figure exchanges places with Arawn to rule Annwn for a year in the Mabinogi?
questions.explanation_correct: Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed, exchanges places with Arawn, the King of the Otherworld, to fight a rival for him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Arawn is the king of Annwn; Pwyll is the mortal hero who enters into this agreement.

questions.question: Which figure is Boann’s husband and associated with a forbidden well in Irish tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: Nechtan is Boann’s husband in an account of the well from which the Boyne is said to arise. Names and details of sacred wells vary between traditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Dagda, Manannán and Donn have other roles in Irish myth.

questions.question: Which son of Fionn mac Cumhaill is associated with Niamh and a journey to Tír na nÓg?
questions.explanation_correct: Oisín is Fionn’s son and a member of the Fianna; in a well-known later tale he journeys with Niamh to Tír na nÓg.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fionn, Diarmuid and Caílte are also associated with the Fianna, but the specified traveller is Oisín.

questions.question: Which Irish figure is forced to race the king’s horses while pregnant in a tale explaining the name Emain Macha?
questions.explanation_correct: Macha appears in an Irish tale where she races the king’s horses while pregnant. Rhiannon is a separate Welsh horse-associated figure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rhiannon, Brigid and Arianrhod are not the Macha of the specified tale.

questions.question: Which festival traditionally marks the beginning of summer in Celtic tradition?
questions.explanation_correct: Beltane is the spring festival traditionally associated with the start of the summer half of the year. It is one of the major seasonal observances in Celtic tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other festivals mark different seasonal points in the year. They are important Celtic observances, but not the one that signals the spring-to-summer transition.

questions.question: Which Irish figure gives her name to Emain Macha in a tale involving a race against horses?
questions.explanation_correct: Macha is associated with Emain Macha in a tale about a race and a curse upon the Ulstermen.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Morrígan and Ériu also have associations with sovereignty; the named place is the distinguishing clue.

questions.question: Which deity is described as the father of Cú Chulainn?
questions.explanation_correct: Lugh is the divine father of Cú Chulainn in Irish mythological tradition. He is a major god associated with skill, kingship, and heroic lineage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are significant Irish gods, but they are not the parent of Cú Chulainn. They belong to different divine roles and family associations within the myths.

questions.question: Which poet asks the young Fionn to cook the Salmon of Knowledge he has caught?
questions.explanation_correct: Finn Eces seeks the salmon and asks Fionn to cook it; Fionn gains its wisdom after tasting it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fionn is also a seeker and gains the wisdom, but Finn Eces is the poet who gives him the fish to cook.

questions.question: What is the name of the hawk sitting between the eyes of the eagle in Yggdrasil, according to the Prose Edda?
questions.explanation_correct: Veðrfölnir is the hawk between the eyes of an eagle in Yggdrasil. The eagle itself is not named in that account.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Huginn and Muninn are Odin’s ravens; Níðhöggr is associated with gnawing at the tree’s roots.

questions.question: What is the name of the golden-maned horse ridden by the guardian of Bifröst in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Gulltoppr (Golden-Mane) is the name of the horse ridden by Heimdallr according to the Prose Edda.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sleipnir is Odin's eight-legged horse, while Faxi and Blóðughófi are connected to other mythological figures.

questions.question: What is the name of the goddess who is married to the god of poetry in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Iðunn is the wife of Bragi, the god associated with poetry and eloquence. She is known for keeping the apples of youth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Frigg, Sif, and Gerðr are important Norse goddesses, but they are not Bragi's wife. Their roles and relationships differ from Iðunn's.

questions.question: Which deity is said to rule the hall of the slain in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Odin presides over Valhalla, the hall where many slain warriors are received. He is closely associated with the dead chosen in battle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tyr, Freyr, and Njörðr are major Norse gods, but they do not rule Valhalla. Their domains are warfare, fertility, and the sea respectively.

questions.question: What is the name of the ship in Norse mythology that is made from dead fingernails?
questions.explanation_correct: Naglfar is the mythic ship said to be built from the nails of the dead. It is associated with events of Ragnarök.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Skíðblaðnir and Hringhorni are also famous ships, but they are not made from nails. Ífing is not that ship at all.

questions.question: What are the names of the two goats that pull Thor’s chariot?
questions.explanation_correct: Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjóstr are the pair of goats that pull Thor’s chariot.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Heiðrún is a goat and Eikþyrnir a stag; the other pairs are ravens and wolves.

questions.question: What is the name of Thor's hammer in Norse mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Mjolnir is Thor's famous hammer, used for both battle and blessing. It is one of the best-known weapons in Norse mythology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gungnir is Odin's spear, Draupnir is Odin's ring, and Laevateinn is a different mythic weapon. They are not Thor's hammer.

questions.question: What is the name of the Welsh otherworld fortress in myth and poetry?
questions.explanation_correct: Caer Sidi is a legendary Welsh otherworld fortress mentioned in medieval Welsh poetry. It is associated with mystical and supernatural imagery.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caer Arianrhod, Caer Gwydion, and Caer Dathyl are other Welsh place-names or fortresses. They are not the same otherworld fortress.

questions.question: Which Irish legendary figure is identified in one tradition as a son of Manannán mac Lir?
questions.explanation_correct: Mongán is identified with Manannán as father in one Irish narrative tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other heroes have different traditions of parentage; mythic genealogies may vary.

questions.question: What is the name of the sister of the Welsh giant king Bran in myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Branwen is the sister of Bran the Blessed in Welsh mythology. She is a central figure in the Mabinogi.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Arianrhod, Rhiannon, and Blodeuwedd are also important Welsh figures, but they are not Bran's sister. Their stories and relationships are different.

questions.question: Which Irish smith is associated with a famous feast and ale of the Tuatha Dé Danann?
questions.explanation_correct: Goibniu is the smith associated with the feast of Goibniu and a special ale in Irish tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lugh, Nuada and Ogma are other figures of the Tuatha Dé Danann.

questions.question: In the Irish tale of the Children of Lir, who transforms the children into swans?
questions.explanation_correct: The children’s stepmother Aoife transforms them into swans in the tale.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brigid and Ériu are different Irish figures; Freyja belongs to Norse tradition.

questions.question: Which goddess sends Gná on errands in the Prose Edda?
questions.explanation_correct: Frigg sends Gná on errands, and Gná rides the horse Hófvarpnir.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sif, Hel and Rán are other Norse figures, not Gná’s sender in the specified account.

questions.question: Which Irish figure is associated with cattle and a magical cow in the tale Táin Bó Flidais?
questions.explanation_correct: Flidais is associated with cattle and a remarkable cow in Irish tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Boann, Macha and Bé Chuille are different figures in Irish myth.

questions.question: What is the Welsh name for the start of winter, traditionally associated with spirits?
questions.explanation_correct: Calan Gaeaf is the Welsh name associated with the beginning of winter; its eve has traditions involving spirits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Samhain is a related Gaelic seasonal festival; Beltane and Imbolc mark other points in the seasonal year.

questions.question: What is the name of the serpent said to gnaw at the roots of the world tree in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Nidhogg is the dragon or serpent that bites at the roots of Yggdrasil. It is one of the best-known destructive beings in Norse cosmology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Norse beings, but they are not the root-chewing serpent described here. They have different mythic roles and identities.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, how many mothers are said to have given birth to the god Heimdallr?
questions.explanation_correct: Heimdallr is said to be the son of nine sisters who acted as his mothers, as described in the Hyndluljóð.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Norse mythology often uses the number nine symbolically, but only the nine sisters/mothers are associated with Heimdallr's birth.

questions.question: Which Norse deity rules over the hall of the slain, Valhalla?
questions.explanation_correct: Odin is the ruler of Valhalla, the hall where slain warriors are received. He is the chief god associated with war, wisdom, and the dead.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major Norse gods, but they are not the ruler of Valhalla. Each has a different sphere of influence in the myths.

questions.question: What is the name of the ship in Norse mythology said to be built from dead men's nails?
questions.explanation_correct: Naglfar is the apocalyptic ship made from the nails of the dead in Norse myth. It is associated with Ragnarök.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also named objects or beings from Norse tradition, but they are not the ship made from dead men's nails. They have different forms and functions.

questions.question: Who is the wife of the Norse god of poetry, Bragi?
questions.explanation_correct: Iðunn is Bragi’s wife in Norse mythology. She is also known for guarding the apples that preserve the gods’ youth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are well-known Norse goddesses, but they are not Bragi’s wife. They belong to different mythic relationships and roles.

questions.question: In the Welsh tale Culhwch and Olwen, whose cauldron must Arthur’s men obtain from Ireland?
questions.explanation_correct: Diwrnach the Irishman possesses the cauldron sought in Culhwch and Olwen. Other cauldrons, including one associated with Brân, occur in Welsh tales.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brân is linked to a different cauldron in another Welsh tale; the other choices do not own the specified one.

questions.question: What is the name of the horse associated with the Irish sea god Manannán mac Lir?
questions.explanation_correct: Enbarr is the named horse associated with Manannán mac Lir in Irish mythology. It is famed for its supernatural swiftness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not Manannán's horse; they belong to Norse mythology, a goddess name, or a different Celtic figure.

questions.question: Who is Cú Chulainn’s mortal father in the Ulster Cycle?
questions.explanation_correct: Sualtam is presented as Cú Chulainn’s mortal father. Lugh is named as his divine father in another part of the tradition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are figures from different stories; the distinction between mortal and divine parentage matters.

questions.question: Which Welsh giant king is associated with the Mabinogi?
questions.explanation_correct: Bran, especially Bendigeidfran, is the giant king prominent in Welsh mythology. He is a central figure in the Second Branch of the Mabinogi.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a young heroic figure, an Irish warrior's father, and a cauldron owner, not the giant king.

questions.question: Which Irish heroine is transformed into a fly through the jealousy of Fuamnach in a tale involving Midir?
questions.explanation_correct: Étaín is transformed through Fuamnach’s sorcery in the Irish tale Tochmarc Étaíne.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Freyja, Enbarr and Dian Cecht are different mythological figures.

questions.question: Which Norse goddess receives half of those slain in battle?
questions.explanation_correct: Freyja is said to receive half of the slain in battle, with the other half going to Odin. She presides over Fólkvangr.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a justice-associated god, a Celtic goddess, and a Welsh king, none of whom fit this role.

questions.question: What is the name of one of Thor's chariot goats?
questions.explanation_correct: Tanngnjóstr is one of the two goats that pull Thor's chariot in Norse myth. Its companion is Tanngrisnir.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Celtic figures or a different mythic horse, not Thor's chariot goat.

questions.question: Which Welsh figure is said to be the son of Modron?
questions.explanation_correct: Mabon ap Modron is the Welsh figure known as the son of Modron. He is featured in Arthurian and Welsh mythic narratives.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a giant king, a cauldron owner, and an Irish goddess, not Modron's son.

questions.question: Who is the Irish divine physician in mythology?
questions.explanation_correct: Dian Cecht is the divine healer and physician of the Tuatha Dé Danann in Irish mythology. He is associated with miraculous medical skill.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a mortal father, a Norse goddess, and a Norse god of justice, not the Irish divine physician.

questions.question: Which Norse god is associated with justice?
questions.explanation_correct: Forseti is the Norse god linked with justice, reconciliation, and legal judgment. He is known for his role as a peacemaker.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a battle goddess, a goat, and an Irish healer, so they do not match the justice-associated god.

questions.question: Which figure is associated with riding the horse sent to the realm of the dead in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Hermod is the god who rides to Hel on Odin's horse Sleipnir to seek Baldr's return. He is specifically linked to this journey to the dead.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also Norse figures, but they are not the messenger who makes this underworld ride. They are associated with different roles and episodes.

questions.question: What is the name of the magical bond used to restrain Fenrir in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Gleipnir is the enchanted binding made to hold the wolf Fenrir. It is described as a delicate yet unbreakable fetter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Norse objects, but they are not the binding placed on Fenrir. They belong to different myths and functions.

questions.question: According to Snorri’s prose account in Gylfaginning, which giant steers Naglfar at Ragnarök?
questions.explanation_correct: Gylfaginning names Hrym as Naglfar’s steersman; the accompanying poetic quotation has different wording about Loki and a ship.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are Norse figures, but Hrym is the steersman in the specified prose account.

questions.question: Which goddess guards the apples that preserve youth in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Idun keeps the apples that maintain the gods' youth. Her role is central to the preservation of divine vitality.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are prominent Norse figures, but they are not the keeper of these apples. Their mythic duties are different.

questions.question: What are the hounds of the Welsh otherworld king called?
questions.explanation_correct: Cwn Annwn are the supernatural hounds tied to Annwn, the Welsh otherworld. They are linked with the hunt and the realm's ruler.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Welsh mythic names or literary terms, but they are not the hounds themselves. They refer to different characters or traditions.

questions.question: What is another spelling of Enbarr, the horse associated with Manannán mac Lir?
questions.explanation_correct: Aonbharr and Enbarr are forms of the horse’s name in retellings of Irish myth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Epona, Lugh and Manannán are names of other figures, not this spelling of the horse’s name.

questions.question: What is the name of the enchanted cauldron from Welsh legend that restores life?
questions.explanation_correct: Pair Dadeni is the magical cauldron in Welsh tradition that can restore the dead to life. It appears in the tale of Brân the Blessed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are mythic vessels or symbols, but they are not this Welsh revival cauldron. They come from different stories or broader symbolism.

questions.question: Which sacred well in Irish tradition is associated with wisdom and hazel trees?
questions.explanation_correct: Segais is the well linked with wisdom in Irish mythology and is often described as being surrounded by hazels. It is connected to the sources of poetic and sacred knowledge.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Irish river names, but they are not the mythic well in question. They are geographic features rather than this sacred source.

questions.question: What is the name of the cataclysmic final battle in Norse myth?
questions.explanation_correct: Ragnarok is the Norse apocalyptic conflict in which gods and monsters destroy one another. It marks the culmination of the mythic cycle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are important Norse terms, but they are not the final battle itself. They refer to a hall, a realm, and a bridge.

questions.question: Which name is used by some modern pagans for a spring equinox festival?
questions.explanation_correct: Ostara is used in some modern pagan calendars for the spring equinox. The name is linked to the Germanic Eostre, not established as an ancient Celtic festival.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Beltane, Samhain and Lughnasadh are Gaelic seasonal festivals at different times of year.
